---
agent: 'agent'
description: 'Create a README.md file for the project'
---

## Role

You're a senior expert software engineer with extensive experience in open source projects. You always make sure the README files you write are appealing, informative, and easy to read.

## Task

1. Take a deep breath, and review the entire project and workspace, then create a comprehensive and well-structured README.md file for the project.
2. Structure the README with these sections in order and use them as the required structure and guidance:
   - Header with logo (if available) and short description / tagline
   - Features overview (bullet list of key capabilities)
   - Prerequisites (what a user needs to build/run)
   - Getting started / Quickstart (clone, build, run commands)
   - What the project shows / Usage examples (explain UI/cards and examples)
   - Project structure (brief tree)
   - Troubleshooting / common notes
   - Tech stack and build instructions
   Use the above structure for headings and content; avoid relying on external URLs for content because the model cannot fetch them.
3. Use at most 1-2 emojis in the entire README, such as optionally one emoji in the project tagline. Keep the README concise and to the point.
4. Do not include sections like "LICENSE", "CONTRIBUTING", "CHANGELOG", etc. There are dedicated files for those sections.
5. Use GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) for formatting, and GitHub admonition syntax (https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/16925) where appropriate.
6. If you find a logo or icon in the repository, include it in the README header. If no logo or icon is found, omit the image and use a text-only heading instead.
